themes.title: Interactions of humans with the environment

themes.title: Social interactions and organization
themes.question: Who had status, opportunities, or obligations?

themes.title: Political systems and governance

themes.title: Economic systems

quiz.title: Unit 4 SAQ 01
quiz.headline: Smith on the discoveries
quiz.prompt: Use the passage below to answer all parts of the question.
quiz.instructions: Answer all three parts. For each part, Answer the question directly, Prove it with specific historical evidence, and Explain how the evidence supports your answer. On the AP exam each part earns one point. This is self-assessment practice, not official College Board scoring.
quiz.note: Original Page One practice in AP short-answer format. Model answers show one strong response; other accurate, well-supported answers can earn the point.

stimulusBlocks.attribution: Adam Smith, Scottish philosopher and economist, An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations, 1776
stimulusBlocks.citation: Adam Smith, An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations, Book IV, ch. 7, part 3. Project Gutenberg eBook #3300.
stimulusBlocks.note: The East Indies and West Indies mean South and Southeast Asia and the Americas. The mercantile system is mercantilism, which Smith criticized.
stimulusBlocks.text:
The discovery of America, and that of a passage to the East Indies by the Cape of Good Hope, are the two greatest and most important events recorded in the history of mankind. . . . By uniting in some measure the most distant parts of the world, by enabling them to relieve one another's wants, to increase one another's enjoyments, and to encourage one another's industry, their general tendency would seem to be beneficial. To the natives, however, both of the East and West Indies, all the commercial benefits which can have resulted from those events have been sunk and lost in the dreadful misfortunes which they have occasioned. . . . At the particular time when these discoveries were made, the superiority of force happened to be so great on the side of the Europeans, that they were enabled to commit with impunity every sort of injustice in those remote countries.

In the mean time, one of the principal effects of those discoveries has been, to raise the mercantile system to a degree of splendour and glory which it could never otherwise have attained to.

scaffold.label: Answer
scaffold.text: Respond directly to the task verb: identify, describe, or explain.

scaffold.label: Prove
scaffold.text: Name a specific person, place, institution, or development.

scaffold.label: Explain
scaffold.text: Show how or why the evidence answers the question.

parts.prompt: Identify ONE effect of the voyages of exploration that Smith describes.
criteria: Names a specific effect stated in the passage.
Connects the effect to the voyages of exploration.

model.answer: Smith says the voyages connected distant parts of the world through trade.
model.prove: He writes that the discoveries united “the most distant parts of the world,” letting them relieve one another's wants and encourage one another's industry.
model.explain: Sea routes to the Americas and around Africa let goods move between regions that had never traded directly, creating a global economy.

parts.alternatives: Answers can also identify the misfortunes suffered by Indigenous peoples, or the strengthening of the mercantile system.

parts.prompt: Explain ONE way European expansion caused the “dreadful misfortunes” Smith describes for the natives of the Americas in the period 1450 to 1750.
criteria: Names a specific development from the period.
Explains how it harmed Indigenous peoples.

model.answer: Spanish labor systems forced Indigenous people into dangerous work for colonial profit.
model.prove: Under the Spanish mit'a, Andean communities had to send men to the silver mines of Potosí, where many died from accidents and mercury poisoning.
model.explain: Because colonial wealth depended on silver, Spain used its power to force Indigenous labor, which Smith calls the “superiority of force” that allowed injustice.

parts.alternatives: Answers can also explain the encomienda system, epidemic disease such as smallpox, or the conquest of the Mexica and Inca.

parts.prompt: Explain ONE way Smith's purpose in writing might affect how historians use this passage.
criteria: Identifies a specific feature of Smith's purpose or point of view.
Explains how it affects the passage's usefulness as evidence.

model.answer: Smith wrote to criticize mercantilism, so he presents colonial trade in a way that supports his case for freer trade.
model.prove: He describes the discoveries raising the mercantile system to “splendour and glory,” a system the rest of his book attacks.
model.explain: Historians can use the passage as evidence of an influential 1776 view, but they should check his economic claims against other evidence because he was making an argument.

parts.alternatives: Answers can also note that Smith wrote in 1776, centuries after the voyages, so the passage reflects later reflection rather than eyewitness experience.
